Its EVM contracts implement EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`, which is why it is the default token of the x402 `exact` scheme, for example on Base. MPP has a separate `usdc` payment method drafted by Circle.
ste: USDC is a US dollar stablecoin from Circle. USDC supports EIP-3009, so x402 uses USDC by default on EVM networks.

plain: AP2 delegation model in which a credential issued to the user signs mandates, typically through OpenID4VP, and verifiers trust the issuer.
ste: A model where a credential of the user signs the mandates.

plain: A Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard contract keeps its state at a fixed address while the logic contract behind it can be replaced. In UUPS the upgrade function lives in the logic contract, so whoever passes `_authorizeUpgrade` can change the code. The deployed ERC-8004 registries are UUPS proxies with upgrade rights restricted to one owner address.
ste: A UUPS proxy is a contract that keeps its address and data when its code changes. The owner of the proxy can replace the code.

plain: The third ERC-8004 registry, where a named validator records a 0 to 100 check of an agent's work. Specified in the Draft text, not officially deployed.
ste: A registry where a validator writes the result of a check. It is not officially on a chain.

plain: A call to the ERC-8004 Validation Registry in which an agent's owner asks a named validator to check a piece of work. The request carries a `requestURI` and a `requestHash`, and only that validator can answer with `validationResponse` and a score from 0 to 100. The Validation Registry is specified, but the contracts README lists no official deployment.
ste: A validation request asks one validator to check the work of an agent. The validator gives a score from 0 to 100.

plain: The number of decimal places (0 to 18) that applies to an ERC-8004 feedback value. An uptime of 99.77% is value 9977 with valueDecimals 2.
ste: The number of decimal places of a feedback value.

plain: The token returned by an ACP Delegate Payment call, shown with a `vt_` prefix in the spec examples. It stands for the stored card and can be used only by the named merchant, for the named checkout session, within the allowance. The agent passes it to the merchant in `payment_data.instrument.credential.token` when it completes checkout.
ste: A vault token is the token that the payment provider returns after delegated payment. The merchant can use the token only within the allowance.

plain: SD-JWT VC claim naming the credential type. AP2 uses it for the mandate type and schema version, for example mandate.payment.1.
ste: The claim that gives the mandate type and version.

plain: A tamper-evident digital claim that an issuer makes about a subject, which anyone can check with the issuer's public key. The W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 is one format, and SD-JWT VC is another; AP2 mandates are issued as SD-JWT credentials. Do not confuse it with an MPP credential, which is a payment proof in an HTTP header.
ste: A verifiable credential is a signed claim that an issuer makes about a subject. A verifier can check the claim with the public key of the issuer.

plain: An open specification from Mastercard (version 0.1-draft, 2026-02-18) for proving what a user authorized an agent to buy, as a chain of SD-JWT credentials. An issuer signs layer 1 about the user's card and key, the user signs layer 2 with a mandate, and in autonomous mode the agent signs layer 3 payment and checkout credentials for the network and the merchant. Its mandate names mirror AP2 v0.2, and Mastercard says it will embed VI in Agent Pay's intent APIs.
ste: Verifiable Intent is a Mastercard specification that proves the purchases that a user lets an agent make. It uses a chain of SD-JWT credentials.

plain: A Mastercard token for web guest checkouts that comes with an expiry date and a one-time DTVC, so an agent can type all three into a normal card form.
ste: A Mastercard token that an agent can put in a usual card form. It comes with a code for one use.

plain: Visa's program and API set for agent commerce, announced on 2025-04-30. It covers agent-specific tokens, cardholder step-up verification and passkey setup, Payment Instructions that bind credential requests to what the user approved, and commerce signals sent back to Visa. Visa presents Trusted Agent Protocol as an enhancement to VIC.
ste: Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) is the Visa program for payments by AI agents. VIC gives tokens, passkeys and payment instructions to agents.

plain: Visa's network tokenization service, which replaces a card number with a token for wallets, merchants and other token requestors. The VIC overview lists VTS APIs among the services that Visa's MCP server reaches. Visa sources for TAP talk about VTS and VIC tokens, not MDES, which is Mastercard's equivalent.
ste: Visa Token Service (VTS) is the Visa service that replaces a card number with a token. The Visa MCP server gives access to VTS APIs.

plain: A signed off-chain message that raises the total a payee may claim from a payment channel. MPP Tempo sessions send vouchers with a rising `cumulativeAmount`, and the x402 `batch-settlement` scheme uses vouchers with `maxClaimableAmount`. Vouchers cost no fees, and only the latest one matters when the channel settles.
ste: A voucher is a signed message that increases the total amount that the payee can claim. The client sends vouchers off the chain, so they cost no fee.

plain: An IETF working group and its draft (`draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00`, posted 2026-09-01) for automated clients that sign their requests with RFC 9421 and publish keys in a directory. It requires the `web-bot-auth` tag and a covered `Signature-Agent` header. Visa TAP predates the draft and does not conform to it, though Cloudflare describes both card networks' schemes as built on Web Bot Auth.
ste: Web Bot Auth is an IETF draft for bots that sign HTTP requests with RFC 9421. The bot publishes its public keys in a directory.

plain: The standard HTTP response header that tells a client how to authenticate. MPP defines a new authentication scheme called `Payment`, so a 402 response carries one or more `WWW-Authenticate: Payment` challenges with `id`, `realm`, `method`, `intent` and `request` parameters. On 2026-10-11 the `Payment` scheme was requested in an Internet-Draft but not yet in the IANA registry.
ste: WWW-Authenticate is the HTTP header that tells the client how to authenticate. In MPP, this header contains the payment challenge.

plain: The field in every x402 message that names the protocol version: 1 for the legacy wire format, 2 for the current one.
ste: A field that gives the protocol version. The value 2 is the current version.

plain: Zero-knowledge machine learning: a proof that a given model produced a given output, which can be checked without rerunning the model. The ERC-8004 spec names zkML proofs as one possible method for validators in its Validation Registry. The spec does not define a zkML format, and the registry has no official deployment.
ste: zkML is a proof that a model gave a specified output. ERC-8004 names zkML as one possible method for validators.
